questions.accessible_text:
1. [Maximum mark: 6]

Let f(x) = √(x + 2) for x ≥ −2 and g(x) = 3x − 7 for x ∈ ℝ.

(a) Write down f(14). [1]

(b) Find (g ∘ f)(14). [2]

(c) Find g⁻¹(x). [3]

2. [Maximum mark: 6]

The following box-and-whisker plot shows the number of text messages sent by students in a school on a particular day.

[Box-and-whisker plot: minimum 0, lower quartile 4, median 9, upper quartile 11 and maximum 39.]

(a) Find the value of the interquartile range. [2]

(b) One student sent k text messages, where k > 11. Given that k is an outlier, find the least value of k. [4]
questions.summary: Use quartiles and the outlier rule.
questions.solution: (a) IQR=11−4=7. (b) The upper fence is 11+1.5(7)=21.5. Since k counts messages, the least possible outlier is k=22.

questions.accessible_text:
3. [Maximum mark: 7]

Consider a function f(x), for −2 ≤ x ≤ 2. The following diagram shows the graph of f.

[Graph: A smooth strictly increasing S-shaped curve starts at (−2,−2), passes through (0,−0.5) and (1,0), and ends at (2,1).]

(a) Write down the value of (i) f(0); (ii) f⁻¹(1). [2]

(b) Write down the range of f⁻¹. [1]

(c) On the grid above, sketch the graph of f⁻¹. [4]
questions.summary: Read and sketch an inverse-function graph.
questions.solution: (a)(i) f(0)=−1/2. (ii) f⁻¹(1)=2. (b) The range is [−2,2]. (c) Reflect the given curve in y=x; it includes (−2,−2), (−1/2,0), (0,1), and (1,2).

questions.accessible_text:
4. [Maximum mark: 7]

Let f(x) = ax² − 4x − c. A horizontal line, L, intersects the graph of f at x = −1 and x = 3.

(a) (i) The equation of the axis of symmetry is x = p. Find p.

(ii) Hence, show that a = 2. [4]

(b) The equation of L is y = 5. Find the value of c. [3]
questions.solution: (a)(i) p=(−1+3)/2=1. (ii) The axis is x=2/a; hence a=2. (b) f(−1)=2+4−c=5, so c=1.

5. [Maximum mark: 7]

Let f(x) = 1/(2x − 1), for x > 1/2.

(a) Find ∫(f(x))² dx. [3]

(b) Part of the graph of f is shown in the following diagram.

[Diagram: The positive decreasing branch y=1/(2x−1), with region R under the curve and above the x-axis between x=1 and x=9 shaded.]

The shaded region R is enclosed by the graph of f, the x-axis, and the lines x = 1 and x = 9. Find the volume of the solid formed when R is revolved 360° about the x-axis. [4]
questions.summary: Integrate and find a volume of revolution.

questions.accessible_text:
6. [Maximum mark: 6]

Six equilateral triangles, each with side length 3 cm, are arranged to form a hexagon. This is shown in the following diagram.

[Diagram not to scale: A regular hexagon is divided from its centre into six equilateral triangles. Vector p goes from the left vertex to the upper-left vertex; q goes from the left vertex horizontally to the centre; r goes from the left vertex to the lower-left vertex.]

The vectors p, q and r are shown on the diagram.

Find p · (p + q + r).
questions.solution: By symmetry p+r=q, so p+q+r=2q. Since |p|=|q|=3 and the angle is 60°, p·(2q)=2(3)(3)cos60°=9.

7. [Maximum mark: 7]

Consider f(x), g(x) and h(x), for x ∈ ℝ where h(x) = (f ∘ g)(x).

Given that g(3) = 7, g′(3) = 4 and f′(7) = −5, find the gradient of the normal to the curve of h at x = 3.
questions.summary: Apply the chain rule and find a normal.

questions.accessible_text:
8. [Maximum mark: 13]

A function f(x) has derivative f′(x) = 3x² + 18x. The graph of f has an x-intercept at x = −1.

(a) Find f(x). [6]

(b) The graph of f has a point of inflexion at x = p. Find p. [4]

(c) Find the values of x for which the graph of f is concave-down. [3]
questions.solution: (a) f=x³+9x²+C and f(−1)=0 gives C=−8, so f=x³+9x²−8. (b) f″=6x+18=0 gives p=−3. (c) f″<0 when x<−3.

9. [Maximum mark: 16]

Point A has coordinates (−4, −12, 1) and point B has coordinates (2, −4, −4).

(a) Show that AB⃗ = (6, 8, −5). [1]

(b) The line L passes through A and B.
(i) Find a vector equation for L.
(ii) Point C(k, 12, −k) is on L. Show that k = 14. [6]

(c) (i) Find OB⃗ · AB⃗.
(ii) Write down the value of angle OBA. [3]

Point D is also on L and has coordinates (8, 4, −9).
(d) Find the area of triangle OCD. [6]

10. [Maximum mark: 15]

The first two terms of an infinite geometric sequence are u₁ = 18 and u₂ = 12sin²θ, where 0 < θ < 2π, and θ ≠ π.

(a) (i) Find an expression for r in terms of θ.
(ii) Find the possible values of r. [5]

(b) Show that the sum of the infinite sequence is 54/(2 + cos(2θ)). [4]

(c) Find the values of θ which give the greatest value of the sum. [6]
questions.solution: (a)(i) r=(2/3)sin²θ. (ii) 0<r≤2/3. (b) S∞=18/[1−(2/3)sin²θ]=54/[2+cos2θ]. (c) The denominator is least when cos2θ=−1, giving θ=π/2 or 3π/2.
